rules.sentence: First-generation antipsychotics: High-potency drugs such as fluphenazine, haloperidol, and trifluoperazine are frequently associated with drug-induced parkinsonism.
Low-potency drugs such as chlorpromazine and thioridazine are also known causes but are less common.
About 80% of individuals taking typical antipsychotics experience extrapyramidal symptoms.
However, risperidone, ziprasidone, and olanzapine are more likely to cause drug-induced parkinsonism compared to quetiapine and clozapine.
